stimuli.title: Seven people live on different floors of a seven-storey building. Floor 1 is the bottom floor, and floor 7 is the top floor.
stimuli.body:
Clues:
1. Varun is exactly 3 positions above Geeta.
2. Tanvi is at floor 5.
3. Ira is exactly 3 positions above Isha.
4. There are exactly 2 positions between Vikram and Geeta.
stimuli.solution: floor 1: Vikram; floor 2: Harish; floor 3: Isha; floor 4: Geeta; floor 5: Tanvi; floor 6: Ira; floor 7: Varun

stimuli.title: Seven people have interviews in seven consecutive months from January to July, one per month.
stimuli.body:
Clues:
1. Aarav is exactly 2 positions later than Om.
2. Aarav is exactly 3 positions later than Chitra.
3. Bhavna is at May.
4. In the stated ordering, Aarav comes before Tarun, and Tarun comes before Ira.
stimuli.solution: January: Chitra; February: Om; March: Ravi; April: Aarav; May: Bhavna; June: Tarun; July: Ira

stimuli.title: Seven employees hold seven distinct ranks (rank 1 is junior-most and rank 7 is senior-most).
stimuli.body:

2. Dev is immediately senior to Ravi.

4. Kavya is exactly 3 positions senior to Yuvraj.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain U = T ≥ P < X ≤ Q, decide which conclusions follow. I: U ≤ T. II: T ≥ X.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is always true and II is not necessarily true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain V ≥ W ≥ S > P < Q, decide which conclusions follow. I: P ≥ Q. II: V > P.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is not necessarily true and II is always true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain U ≥ W < T ≤ R < Z, decide which conclusions follow. I: U = T. II: R ≥ Z.

questions.explanation: Exhaustive valid-order checking confirms: I is not necessarily true and II is not necessarily true.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain W < S ≥ X < Z ≥ R, decide which conclusions follow. I: S > R. II: W ≤ R.

questions.stem: Given the inequality chain U < V ≤ Q < R < Z, decide which conclusions follow. I: Q ≤ Z. II: U ≥ Z.

questions.stem: Statements: Some painters are workers. Some workers are coders. Conclusions: I. Some painters are coders. II. All coders are painters. Which conclusion follows?

questions.explanation: A is contained in B, while B and C are disjoint.

questions.stem: Ritu walks 75 km north, then 60 km east, then 15 km south and finally 15 km west. What is her shortest distance from the starting point?

questions.stem: A cyclist travels 135 km north, 60 km east, 75 km south and 15 km west. What total distance did the cyclist travel?
